recognize_zh: 低倍下紅血球不是一條條疊成錢串狀，而是聚成大小不一、形狀不規則的團塊，散布整個抹片，這種不規則聚集就是紅血球凝集（agglutination），配合臨床即為冷凝集素病的典型抹片表現。
features: Diffuse irregular, three-dimensional clumps of red cells of varying size throughout the smear
Clumps have irregular, grape-like outlines rather than linear stacked (coin-like) chains
Free single red cells interspersed between aggregates
Scattered leukocytes and platelets without obvious abnormality at this low magnification
Low magnification limits evaluation of individual red cell morphology (e.g., spherocytes, polychromasia)
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low power shows extensive red cell agglutination, with red cells forming numerous irregular, variably sized three-dimensional clumps distributed throughout the smear, interspersed with single free red cells. The aggregates lack the linear, stacked-coin arrangement of rouleaux. Leukocytes and platelets are present without evident abnormality, although individual red cell morphology cannot be assessed at this magnification. Findings are consistent with red cell agglutination due to cold agglutinins, as in primary cold agglutinin disease; correlation with a direct antiglobulin test (C3d positive) and cold agglutinin titer is recommended, and a smear prepared from a prewarmed sample should disperse the clumps.

ddx.dx: Rouleaux formation (e.g., plasma cell myeloma, inflammation)
ddx.vs: Rouleaux form linear stacks of red cells resembling coins with a blue proteinaceous background, whereas agglutinates are irregular clumps that do not disperse with saline but do with warming.
Warm AIHA typically shows spherocytes and polychromasia with IgG-positive DAT and little agglutination, whereas cold agglutinins cause prominent agglutination that disappears at 37 C.
In thick areas red cells overlap diffusely without discrete clumps separated by clear spaces, and the monolayer area of the slide appears normal.
